name: Axis Meridian Corporate Rain Shell
description:
A clean, corporate-issue waterproof shell in charcoal grey with a subtle herringbone texture in the fabric weave, a single chest pocket, and a packable hood that stows into the collar. The Axis Meridian logo — a small geometric mark — appears at the left chest in tonal embroidery. This is the jacket you receive on your first week at an Axis Meridian subsidiary, along with your access card and your orientation packet. It's not exciting. It's not meant to be.

The shell is technically competent — fully seam-sealed, breathable membrane, adjustable cuffs — and utterly anonymous. It marks you as an Axis employee to other Axis employees and as a mid-corporate drone to everyone else. People wear it because it's free and it works. Some people wear it for years after leaving the company because it's still the best rain jacket they own and they've stopped caring what the logo says.
what_it_says: You work for a corporation, or you used to. You're practical about it. The jacket works.
worn_by: anyone who received one and kept it
story_hooks: A character finds an Axis Meridian rain shell in their apartment that doesn't belong to them — the access card sewn into the inner pocket still works on a door they've never tried to open.

A flood of Axis Meridian shells has appeared on Shelf-district secondhand markets, all from the same production run — someone liquidated an entire warehouse's worth, and Axis wants to know who and why.
Wearing this jacket gets a character waved through an Axis checkpoint without scanning — the guard assumes they're staff. The question is how deep they can go before someone looks closer.

physical_description.visual_profile: A minimalist corporate silhouette—structured but not rigid, designed to layer seamlessly over business casual or tech wear. The jacket reads as institutional efficiency; it disappears into a professional wardrobe without demanding attention. On the wearer, it creates a clean vertical line with subtle shoulder definition.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed but tailored through the torso; enough room for layering without blousing. Sleeves taper slightly at the wrist with adjustable friction cuffs. Length hits mid-hip, corporate-standard for mobility and desk work.
physical_description.primary_material: High-grade synthetic shell with bonded breathable membrane. Charcoal grey base with a technical herringbone weave that catches light subtly—not matte, not glossy, intentionally neutral.
physical_description.texture: The herringbone creates micro-texture that reads as quality without ostentation. Smooth to touch but with micro-grip under fingertips. Seams are sealed and flat; no visible stitching interrupts the minimal aesthetic.
physical_description.color_scheme: Charcoal grey (approximately #3a3a3c), entirely monochromatic except for the tonal embroidered Axis Meridian geometric logo at left chest—barely visible unless light hits it directly.
physical_description.closures: Full front zip with a subtle pull tab. Magnetic storm flap overlay covers the zip for a seamless front profile. Adjustable cuff tabs with friction-fit closures—no excess hardware.
distinctive_features: Packable hood stowed into collar—deploys from a seam, not a zipper pocket
Single chest pocket with internal RF-blocking liner (standard corpo anti-surveillance feature)
Tonal embroidered Axis Meridian geometric mark—small enough to be corporate discretion, visible enough to signal affiliation
Subtle herringbone texture weave distinguishes it from generic rain shells
Adjustable cuffs designed for subcutaneous augmentation compatibility (no tight wrist closure that would interfere with implants)
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 1-2 corporate issue. The jacket itself is high-quality (Φ240+ retail value), but its ubiquity and institutional origin signal mid-tier corpo employment, not wealth or status.
physical_description.cultural_context: Marks the wearer as Axis Meridian employee, current or former. In the GLMZ, this signals stability, desk work, and middle-management proximity. Street-side, it reads as 'corporate drone' without judgment—a neutral uniform. Many wear it long after leaving Axis because the quality justifies the logo; wearing it becomes an ironic statement about corporate loyalty or simple practicality.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine on first issue. After months of use, develops minor creasing at elbows and shoulders, scuff marks on cuffs from wrist-mounted augmentation interfaces. Many worn examples show fading of the tonal logo through repeated wear and cleaning. Some have collar wear where the hood is repeatedly deployed. A well-kept specimen shows almost no signs of age due to synthetic durability.
